explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Ahab, king of Samaria, says, “Give me your vineyard to use as a vegetable garden, since it is next to my palace.” A whole palace, and he's still eyeing the lot next door. It's like me owning a bakery and sizing up the empty space next to it for more counter room.

A threshing floor is where grain gets worked, and Ahab never mentions one. He says he wants the vineyard “…to use as a vegetable garden…” The only reason he gives is that it's next to his palace. It's an easy mix-up with all that farm talk, and I once mixed up salt and sugar, so I'm in no position to judge.

Olives are a fair guess, but the king never says a word about them. His plan is the vineyard “…to use as a vegetable garden…” He also points out that it's right next to his palace. A king with a whole palace, servants, the works, and he wants to grow his own vegetables? You know that guy has one sad little tomato plant, and he checks on it every morning like it's a newborn baby.

Silver it is, baker. Ahab gives Naboth two choices: a better vineyard in its place, or if Naboth prefers, the vineyard's value in silver. Naboth is the vineyard's owner, and he answers, “The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.” Silver, a better vineyard, take your pick, and the man still says no. A king standing at your door with a blank check, and you just say no! I can't even say no to a second helping of my own dough.

Gold sounds fancy, but it never shows up in this offer. Ahab says he'll give Naboth a better vineyard, or if Naboth prefers, the value in silver. Silver is the metal on the table. Gold stays in the vault.

Cattle never come up. The king offers Naboth a better vineyard in its place, or if Naboth prefers, its value in silver. Paying for a vineyard with a herd would've meant a whole lot of mooing on the way to the palace.

explanations.answer: It's the inheritance of his fathers
explanations.explanation: That's his reason, friend. Naboth says, “The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.” (1 Kings 21:3) He doesn't haggle or ask for time to think. Me, I might have asked what the better vineyard looked like, so Naboth is a stronger man than I am.

explanations.answer: The king's offer is far too low
explanations.explanation: Naboth never complains about the offer. Ahab put a better vineyard or silver on the table, and Naboth doesn't argue over the price at all. His reason is, “The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.” (1 Kings 21:3) The vineyard is something handed down, not something he's shopping around.

explanations.answer: He already promised it to his son
explanations.explanation: No son is mentioned here. The text gives only one reason, and it's in Naboth's own words: “The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.” (1 Kings 21:3) The vineyard came down to him from his fathers. That's all Naboth says.
Eat is right, baker. Ahab lies down on his bed, turns his face away and refuses to eat. I'd wave a cookie under his nose, but I think this one needed more than that.
Close, since he's in bed. But the text never says he refused to sleep. It says he lay down, turned his face away and refused to eat. Eating is the thing he turned down.
Ahab's face is turned away, but the text never says he refuses to speak. When Jezebel asks what's wrong, he answers her and tells her all about Naboth (1 Kings 21:6). The thing he refuses is food.

Naboth did say that to Ahab. He said it when he told the king no (1 Kings 21:3). But look at how Ahab retells it to Jezebel. He leaves that part out, and the text records him quoting Naboth as saying only, “I will not give you my vineyard!”

Right, it's false. Naboth told Ahab that the vineyard was “…the inheritance of my fathers.” (1 Kings 21:3). But when Ahab tells Jezebel, he only reports Naboth saying, “I will not give you my vineyard!” That part about his fathers never makes it into the retelling.

explanations.answer: She will get him Naboth's vineyard
explanations.explanation: That's the promise, friend. Jezebel, Ahab's wife, tells him, “…I will get you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.” Ahab is lying there with his face turned away, and she walks in and promises him a whole vineyard. That's a lot of confidence for one visit.

explanations.answer: She will find him a better vineyard
explanations.explanation: A better vineyard was Ahab's own offer to Naboth (1 Kings 21:2), not Jezebel's promise. Jezebel, Ahab's wife, tells him, “…I will get you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.” She wants Naboth's vineyard itself, not a swap. It's a mix-up that's easy to make.

An apology is small stuff next to what she promises. Jezebel, Ahab's wife, says, “…I will get you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.” She skips right past sorry and goes for the whole vineyard. That's a bold way to cheer up a sulking husband.

True, baker. Jezebel writes the letters in Ahab's name, seals them with his seal, and sends them to the elders and nobles who lived with Naboth in his city. Jezebel wrote them, but they carry Ahab's name and Ahab's seal. The leaders of Naboth's city got letters that looked like they came from the king.

It's true, though. The text says Jezebel wrote the letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent them to the elders and nobles who lived with Naboth in his city. Those leaders are the ones the letters were sent to.

That's the word, baker. Jezebel's letters say to “…seat two scoundrels opposite him…” (1 Kings 21:10). It's right there in the instructions, plain as can be. Those two men are sitting across from Naboth for a reason.
No priests in this part. The letters say to “…seat two scoundrels opposite him…” (1 Kings 21:10) Those two men are the ones set up across from Naboth. The letters name them scoundrels.
No soldiers here either. Jezebel's letters say to “…seat two scoundrels opposite him…” (1 Kings 21:10) Scoundrels are the word the text uses for those two men.

explanations.answer: Cursing both God and the king
explanations.explanation: That's what the letters say. The two men are to testify, “You have cursed both God and the king!” (1 Kings 21:10) Jezebel's plan has them say it in front of everyone. It's a heavy charge, baker.
Stealing never comes up. The letters tell the two men to testify, “You have cursed both God and the king!” (1 Kings 21:10) The charge is about cursing. Nobody mentions the palace's silver.

No boundary stone in this passage. The letters tell the two men to testify, “You have cursed both God and the king!” (1 Kings 21:10) That's the accusation in the letters. Nothing about neighbors or property lines.

True. The elders and nobles of Naboth's city “…did as Jezebel had instructed in the letters she had written to them.” (1 Kings 21:11) They followed the letters, step by step. This is a heavy part of the story, baker.

It's true, sadly. The text says the elders and nobles of Naboth's city “…did as Jezebel had instructed in the letters she had written to them.” (1 Kings 21:11) They carried out what the letters said. This is a heavy part of the story.

explanations.answer: Go take possession of the vineyard
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Jezebel, Ahab's wife, tells him, “Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite…” Naboth, the vineyard's owner, is gone, and she points her husband straight at the land. I think it's a hard thing to read.

No burial comes up in her words. Jezebel, Ahab's wife, tells him, “Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite…” She does say Naboth is dead, but she never mentions a burial. What she points Ahab to is the vineyard.

Silver does come up, but not as payment. Jezebel says Naboth “…refused to give it to you for silver.” Her order to Ahab is “Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite…” Nothing in that order says to pay Naboth's family.

True, baker. The text says Ahab “…got up and went down to take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.” This is the same king who lay on his bed with his face turned away (1 Kings 21:4). He's moving now. I think this part of the story hurts.
It's true, baker. The text says Ahab “…got up and went down to take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.” He doesn't stay in bed this time. He walks right down to the vineyard.

explanations.answer: Go down and meet King Ahab
explanations.explanation: Right, friend. The LORD tells Elijah the Tishbite, God's prophet, “Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria.” He also tells Elijah where to find him: in Naboth's vineyard, where Ahab has gone to take possession of it. So Elijah's errand is a face-to-face meeting.

explanations.answer: Hide from Jezebel in the hills
explanations.explanation: No hiding in this passage. The LORD tells Elijah the Tishbite, God's prophet, “Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria.” That's a trip toward the king. It's the opposite of staying out of sight.

The elders aren't part of Elijah's orders. The LORD tells Elijah the Tishbite, God's prophet, “Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria.” The instruction names one person to meet, and that's Ahab.

explanations.answer: Dogs will lick up Ahab's blood where they licked Naboth's
explanations.explanation: That's the message. The LORD says, “In the place where the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth, there also the dogs will lick up your blood…” He names the place where the dogs licked up Naboth's blood, and says Ahab's blood will be licked up there too. It's a heavy word, baker.

explanations.answer: Naboth's sons will take back their land from Ahab
explanations.explanation: No sons show up in this message. The LORD says, “In the place where the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth, there also the dogs will lick up your blood…” The second message is about Ahab's own blood. Nobody takes the land back.

explanations.answer: Fire will burn Ahab's palace in Jezreel
explanations.explanation: No fire in this message. The LORD says, “In the place where the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth, there also the dogs will lick up your blood…” The word is about dogs and the place where Naboth's blood was licked up. The palace isn't mentioned.

True. After Ahab says, “So you have found me out, my enemy.” Elijah replies, “I have found you out because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the LORD.” Elijah gives the reason straight.

It's true, friend. Ahab calls Elijah his enemy, and Elijah answers, “I have found you out because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the LORD.” Elijah gives that reason right to the king's face. He doesn't dodge it.

explanations.answer: Ahab provoked His anger and caused Israel to sin
explanations.explanation: That's the reason, baker. The LORD says, “…because you have provoked My anger and caused Israel to sin.” (1 Kings 21:22) Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah are the two houses He compares Ahab's to. The LORD gives His reason, and it's about Ahab's own actions.

explanations.answer: Ahab trusted his army instead of the LORD
explanations.explanation: The army never comes up. The LORD says, “…because you have provoked My anger and caused Israel to sin.” (1 Kings 21:22) That's His stated reason. Nothing about soldiers.

explanations.answer: Ahab refused to listen to the prophet Elijah
explanations.explanation: Not what the text says. The LORD gives His reason: “…because you have provoked My anger and caused Israel to sin.” (1 Kings 21:22) Ahab calls Elijah his enemy, but that isn't the reason the LORD gives. It's about the anger and the sin.

Jezreel is right. The LORD says, “The dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.” Jezebel is Ahab's wife, and the LORD speaks about her too. It's the same city where Naboth's vineyard sits. This is a heavy word, baker.

Samaria does show up in this passage, since Ahab is its king (1 Kings 21:1). But the LORD's word about Jezebel names another place: “The dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.” Jezebel is Ahab's wife. Jezreel is the city of the vineyard.
Jericho isn't in this passage at all. The LORD says, “The dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.” Jezebel is Ahab's wife. Jezreel is the city where Naboth's vineyard sits.

Sackcloth, baker. The text says Ahab “…tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and fasted.” Ahab heard every word from Elijah, and then he acted. This is the same king who called Elijah his enemy earlier in this passage.
Ahab isn't suiting up for a fight. The text says he “…tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and fasted.” His clothes get torn, and sackcloth goes on. Armor would've been a very different scene.
Royal robes are the opposite of what happens. The text says Ahab “…tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and fasted.” He tears his clothes and puts on sackcloth. The king isn't dressing up at all.

Not quite, friend. The LORD asks Elijah, “Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before Me?” The LORD uses that very word, humbled. Then He adds, “Because he has humbled himself before Me, I will not bring the calamity during his days…”

Right, it's false. The LORD says to Elijah, “Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before Me?” He goes on, “Because he has humbled himself before Me, I will not bring the calamity during his days…” So the LORD Himself says Ahab humbled himself.

explanations.answer: It will come on his house in his son's days
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The LORD says, “…I will not bring the calamity during his days, but I will bring it upon his house in the days of his son.” So Ahab's humbling changes when it comes, and the word about his house stays. It's a serious word, and it's worth reading slowly.

explanations.answer: It will never come on his house at all
explanations.explanation: Not quite. The LORD says, “…I will not bring the calamity during his days, but I will bring it upon his house in the days of his son.” The calamity still comes upon Ahab's house. The change is in the timing.

explanations.answer: It will fall only on Jezebel instead
explanations.explanation: The LORD doesn't say that. He says, “…I will not bring the calamity during his days, but I will bring it upon his house in the days of his son.” Jezebel got her own word earlier (1 Kings 21:23). This one is about Ahab's house.
